verses.text: Right then, the disciples came to Jesus: “Who’s the greatest in Heaven’s Kingdom?”
Jesus called a little child over and stood the child among them.
He said, “I’m telling you the truth: unless you turn around and become like little children, you won’t enter Heaven’s Kingdom.
“Whoever humbles themselves like this child is the greatest in Heaven’s Kingdom.
“Whoever welcomes a child like this in my name welcomes me.
“But whoever trips up one of these little ones who believe in me would be better off with a huge millstone tied around their neck and sunk deep in the sea.
“How terrible for the world, because things that make people stumble will come. They have to come, but how terrible for the person who brings them!
“If your hand or foot makes you stumble, cut it off and throw it away. Better to enter life maimed or disabled than keep both hands and feet and be thrown into the everlasting fire.
“If your eye makes you stumble, tear it out and throw it away. Better to enter life with one eye than keep both and be thrown into fiery Gehenna.
“Don’t look down on even one of these little ones. Their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father in heaven.
“The Son of Man came to save the lost.”
“What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one wanders off, won’t he leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go search for the one that wandered?
“If he finds it, I’m telling you the truth: he rejoices over that one more than over the ninety-nine that didn’t wander away.
“In the same way, your Father in heaven doesn’t want even one of these little ones to perish.
“If your brother sins against you, go talk to him privately and point out what he did. If he listens, you’ve won your brother back.
“If he won’t listen, take one or two others with you, so every matter can be confirmed by two or three witnesses.
“If he refuses to listen to them, bring it before the church. If he won’t listen to the church either, treat him like a Gentile or a tax collector.
“I’m telling you the truth: whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven.
“Again, I’m telling you: if two of you on earth agree about anything you ask for, my Father in heaven will do it for you.
“Where two or three gather in my name, I’m there among them.”
Then Peter came and asked him, “Lord, how many times should I forgive my brother when he sins against me? Seven times?”
Jesus answered, “I’m not saying seven times, but seventy times seven.
“That’s why Heaven’s Kingdom is like a king who decided to settle accounts with his servants.
“When he started settling up, they brought him a servant who owed ten thousand talents.
“The servant couldn’t pay. So his master ordered him sold, along with his wife, children, and everything he owned, to cover the debt.
“The servant fell down before him and begged, ‘Please be patient with me. I’ll pay you everything!’
“The master felt compassion, released the servant, and forgave the debt.
“But that servant went out and found a fellow servant who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him by the throat and demanded, ‘Pay me what you owe!’
“His fellow servant fell down and begged, ‘Please be patient with me. I’ll pay you back!’
“But he refused. He went and put him in prison until he paid what he owed.
“When the other servants saw what happened, they were deeply upset. They went and told their master everything.
“Then his master called him in. ‘You wicked servant! I forgave your whole debt because you begged me.
“‘Shouldn’t you have shown mercy to your fellow servant just as I showed mercy to you?’
“His master was furious and handed him over to the torturers until he paid everything he owed.
“My Father in heaven will do the same to each of you unless you forgive your brother sincerely, from your heart.”
